BiblicalUsage: marʼâh is a vision, the sight God gives, and it is also a mirror. In Numbers 12:6 God says He will make Himself known to a prophet in a vision and speak to him in a dream, and in Ezekiel 1:1 the heavens are opened and Ezekiel sees visions of God. In Daniel 10:7 Daniel alone sees the vision while the men with him flee in fear, and in Genesis 46:2 God speaks to Israel in the visions of the night. The word is God showing, not man imagining.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marʼâh shows me that God speaks in visions to those He has chosen. I hold that a true vision always agrees with His written word.
